A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same PCCoT research, with matching authors, method, and main experiments. Their text, equations, tables, figures, and complete appendices support reliable comparison.

before.justification: V1 reports original GPT-2 and Llama experiments, training and inference timings, and latent-token analyses in Section 4 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds chat-template results in Appendix B.7 and an additional iteration configuration in Figure 3.

M1.justification: The parallel Jacobi updates, latent-token construction, answer generation, and CODI-based training remain unchanged. Calling the iteration nonlinear clarifies terminology without changing the procedure.

E1.justification: Appendix C.2 newly reports exploratory experiments on CLUTRR, CommonsenseQA, and StrategyQA, extending beyond the retained GSM8K-Aug and GSM8K-Aug-NL coverage. These additional experiments are reported only qualitatively.

E2.justification: The comparator memberships in Tables 1, 2, and 4 are unchanged, including the internally trained baselines and literature results for CODI, Coconut, and iCoT. The chat-template experiment compares PCCoT configurations rather than introducing another baseline method.

E3.justification: V2 adds evaluation with versus without chat templates and a c = T = 24 configuration in Figure 3. Existing splits, training budgets, and main model configurations remain unchanged; the expanded timing description documents the existing measurement.

E4.justification: New Appendix B.7 tests sensitivity to chat-template use, while Figure 3 extends the iteration analysis to T = 24. The existing convergence, similarity, initialization, decoding, and attention analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions specify three random runs with seeds 0, 1, and 2 and report means with standard deviations. The added results follow that reporting practice; no new uncertainty procedure or formal significance test is documented.

E6.justification: New Table 5 reports chat-template accuracies of 52.24 ± 1.14 on GSM8K and 51.76 ± 0.37 on GSM8K-NL, alongside retained no-template values of 53.35 ± 0.18 and 50.72 ± 1.39. Figure 3 adds the c = T = 24 result, and Appendix C.2 reports no distinguishable performance among approaches on three additional datasets. Existing Tables 1–4 retain their values.

T1.justification: The method equations and Appendix A's Theorem 1 and induction proof are unchanged, including equivalence to continuous CoT when T ≥ c.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: parallel latent reasoning, comparable or better accuracy, nearly 50% training and inference time savings, and improved training stability.

C2.justification: V2 tentatively attributes differing chat-template effects to natural-language versus equation-form reasoning and the inconclusive additional-dataset results to limited training samples. It also relates 24 latent tokens to the reported average of 20.32 explicit reasoning tokens. Existing mechanism uncertainties and limitations remain.

D1.justification: V2 discloses that the main Llama experiments omit chat templates, identifies the timing sample as 100 test examples averaging 105 tokens, and adds dataset-format examples in Appendix D. Conversely, it removes v1's footnote explaining that the cited CODI result uses the Llama base model instead of the instruct model.

R1.justification: V2 adds Cheng and Van Durme's CCoT reference and references for CLUTRR, CommonsenseQA, and StrategyQA, and corrects the CODI attribution in related work. The central positioning relative to continuous CoT and Jacobi decoding remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 removes repetitive introductory wording, makes local terminology and grammar corrections, and adds acknowledgements, Appendix B.7, expanded Appendix C.2 explanations, and Appendix D examples. Most prose and the overall narrative structure are retained.

P2.justification: V2 adds the chat-template table, updates Figure 3's plotted content, legend, and annotations, and clarifies Figure 1's dashed-box caption. Some existing displays move or are renumbered, while the other figures and table structures remain substantially unchanged.

improvement.justification: The chat-template ablation, additional iteration result, and clearer timing and dataset documentation modestly improve empirical support and reproducibility. These gains outweigh the limited loss of transparency from removing the CODI model-variant caveat. The additional datasets lack detailed results, and the central findings and unresolved mechanism limitations remain unchanged.
